AM8F-01.note: 11 is the squaring-the-sign error (4*4 - 6 + 1); -9 drops the square. Standard opener.

AM8F-02.note: 16 = g(4)-g(3), 46 = g(4)+g(2), 56 = g(5)-g(2). All off-by-one-column reads.

AM8F-03.note: 22.5 is the amount burned rather than the time; 3 = 7.5/2.5.

AM8F-04.note: -7 is the linear coefficient, i.e. the student who reaches for the wrong term.

AM8F-05.note: 48 = 8 + 8(5) is the classic n-1 slip and is present. Same habit as AM8F-22.

AM8F-06.note: 49 = 25 + 24 keeps the fixed fee, which is the intended miss. 85 = C(150).

AM8F-07.note: 13 = f(g(3)) is the order-reversal and is offered. Good set for an early item.

AM8F-08.solved: (x-3)^2 >= 0, so the minimum of f is 5 at x = 3.
AM8F-08.note: 3 is the x-coordinate of the vertex reported as the value; 14 = f(0).

AM8F-09.note: 11 is c itself - the stop-too-early answer - and is offered.

AM8F-11.note: 28 is the numerator alone; 6 = (48-12)/6 uses the x=0 row.

AM8F-12.note: 45 is the total bill and 32 = 800(0.04); the stem says 'for the minutes used beyond 300', so 20 is unambiguous.

AM8F-13.note: The 'every term is positive' clause is what closes off r = -3, and it is stated - so the ratio sign is given, not withheld.

AM8F-14.note: Already factored, so this is one step. 8 = 3+5 sign slip, -15/15 are the constant-term reads.

AM8F-15.note: 4800 = 400*3*4 (multiply instead of exponentiate); 97,200 = 5 triplings. Same habit as AM8F-16 and AM8F-24.

AM8F-16.note: 3 is the number of halvings reported as hours; 48 = 8*6. Clean.

AM8F-17.note: The option set is the full 2x2 of both sign choices, which is the right way to build this.

AM8F-18.solved: Undefined where x^2 - 9 = 0, i.e. x = 3 or x = -3. Only 3 is offered.
AM8F-18.note: -5 zeroes the numerator, which is the intended miss. -9 and 9 are weakish - nothing produces them but 'the 9 in the formula'.

AM8F-19.solved: sin x ranges over [-1,1], so least value is 4(-1) + 3 = -1.
AM8F-19.note: -7 = -4-3 (sign applied to the constant too); 7 is the maximum; -4 is the amplitude alone.

AM8F-20.note: 23 = h(4) is the answer-the-wrong-function trap; 51 = f(h(4)).

AM8F-21.solved: g(x) = 0 means f(x) = 10, which happens at x = -3 and x = 2. Greatest is 2.
AM8F-21.note: 'gives EVERY value of the function f' is doing real work here and is correctly stated; without it the item would be broken. -3 is the other solution, 10 is the f-value.

AM8F-22.note: 25 = 50/2 (treating the two terms as equal), 17 = a3. Near-neighbour of AM8F-05.

AM8F-23.note: 5 (the axis of symmetry) is the trap. Not hard: the stem's own sentence 'f(3) = f(k)' is a solvable equation as written, so no symmetry insight is required.

AM8F-24.note: 25,000 is the arithmetic midpoint and 22,500 is half of 45,000 - both good. 'grows by the same percent each year' names the geometric model outright, which is why I do not read this as hard.

AM8F-25.solved: f is zero only at 9, so f(3x-6) = 0 requires 3x - 6 = 9 -> x = 5.
AM8F-25.note: Closest of the non-hard items to hard: 'only at x = 9' hands the student the uniqueness, so what remains is the standard set-the-argument-equal move. 27, 15, 1 cover the three wrong directions.

AM8F-26.solved: 12/(x-4) is an integer when (x-4) divides 12. For 0 <= x <= 10, x-4 runs over -4..6 excluding 0, and -4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4,6 all divide 12 (5 does not). That is 9 values of x: 0,1,2,3,5,6,7,8,10.
AM8F-26.note: HARD, and the withheld notice is real: 'divides 12' includes the negative divisors, which the stem never hints at. The habit answer - list 1,2,3,4,6,12 - gives 5, and 5 is offered as B. 10 is the forgot-to-drop-x=9 count.

AM8F-27.note: HARD. The stem gives only the recurrence g(x+6) = g(x); that periodicity lets you reduce 50 mod 6, and that it runs BACKWARD as well as forward for g(-2), are both unsaid. 18 = 9+9 is the answer of a student who maps both arguments to 2.

AM8F-28.solved: 19.25 - 8.00 = 11.25; 11.25/1.25 = 9 charged increments. Nine increments cover any weight in (11, 12], so the greatest possible weight is 12.
AM8F-28.note: HARD, and the best item in the batch. 'or part of a pound' makes the charge a ceiling function, and 'greatest possible' asks for the top of an interval - neither step is named. Executing the stem linearly gives 3 + 9 = 12 only if you notice the ceiling; the plain arithmetic gives 9, which is offered as D. This is the one item whose template-habit answer is a distractor.
